One common interpretation of this riddle is that when nearly everyone leaves a social gathering (which is the rational, practical thing to do), the fact that one person stays behind is less understandable – i.e. “irrational.” Since both George and Barbara stayed, the riddle asks us to pick one of them as the one acting irrationally. Many find that George’s behavior is the more inexplicable of the two, so option 2 (George) is taken as the answer.

There's a hidden word‐play in the wording. When the question asks, “Who was acting irrationally?” it isn’t necessarily about temper or behavior—it’s a pun based on the math term “irrational.” In mathematics “rational” numbers are those that can be written as a ratio, whereas “irrational” numbers can’t. One of the names subtly alludes to “NaN” (“not a number”), a term familiar to computer programmers. The name “Nancy” hints at that idea, so (1) Nancy is the witty answer.
